message.reasoning:
I'm working out the domain: lekid acts as a marker that moves between nodes via filef or qaceb, requiring a cajif edge connecting them in either direction. So essentially lekid propagates along cajif-connected nodes, and I need to figure out how to move it to reach various target nodes.

Each cahej object has two requirements: a "neleg" action at one node that sets caret, and a "tiqin" action at another node that requires caret to set dodah. So for every object, I need to visit its neleg-location before its tiqin-location, since lekid only exists at one place at a time and travels through a chain-like sequence of connected nodes (bonov through barug).

Looking closer, all the pairwise connections actually cover every combination i<j in that order, forming a complete forward DAG. But the backward-moving relation also exists for every earlier-later pair, meaning lekid can freely move both forward and backward between any two nodes in the sequence, not just adjacent ones -- essentially giving free movement across the whole line of nodes.

Now I'm cataloging each cahej's required neleg and tiqin locations so I can plan visits: for instance hejuq needs barug then xopar, jowot needs mucow then bonov, qamap needs barug then tobah, and so on through the full list including memov, nigig, solah, zomis, qocis, dezeq, cinam, xopob, xocir, lekev, suhow, tofaz, zomim, qumak, sebir, and wegoq, tracking the specific location pairs tied to each.

Since caret must be set at a cahej's neleg location before zurub can happen at its tiqin location, my strategy is to do two full passes: first visiting every relevant node to set carets via riwic, then a second sweep doing zurub actions once carets are already in place. I'm mapping out the visiting order — starting at bonov, then xopar, mucow, vecex, rehax, worun, kutaf, and baxuz — grouping the riwic actions by which cahejs share each neleg location.

I'm continuing that first pass through tobah, vehat, and barug, then working out the second pass where I match each cahej's tiqin location to the correct zurub action, before piecing together the full step-by-step movement plan across all eleven nodes.

Now I realize I can shortcut the return trip: instead of stepping backward node by node, I can use qaceb to jump directly from barug back to bonov in one action, since the cajif connection already exists between them.

From bonov, I retrace the same forward path—jowot, xopar, mucow, vecex, rehax, worun, kutaf, baxuz, tobah, vehat, barug—applying the zurub action at each node to satisfy all the remaining dodah goals not yet completed on the first pass. That covers all 19 goals, so now I'm double-checking that every cahej action was applied exactly once with the correct parameters.

Everything checks out—each of the 19 goals has its riwic and zurub actions correctly paired with matching source and target nodes. I'm ready to assemble the complete plan.
